papers.title: Intrinsically ultralow thermal conductivity in all-inorganic superatomic bulk crystals
papers.abstract: Superatomic compounds, composed of atomic clusters interwoven by weak chemical bonds exhibit large anharmonicity vibrations, are excellent candidates for ultralow thermal conductivity (\k{appa}) materials. However, growing bulk superatomic single crystals is challenging due to complex chemical composition and chemical bonds, and studies on their intrinsic thermal property are scarce. Here, we grew high-quality superatomic single crystals of Re6Se8Te7 and Re6Te15, both of which are narrow band gap semiconductors that change into metals under external physical pressure. At room-temperature, the \k{appa} are 0.32 W m-1 K-1 and 0.53 W m-1 K-1 in Re6Se8Te7 and Re6Te15, respectively, ranking among the lowest value reported in all-inorganic bulk crystals. It is mainly attributed to the large Grüneisen parameter (1.93) and low average sound speed (< 1482 m/s), which are due to soft Te7 nets weakly embedded among the rigid Re6Se8 (Re6Te8) quasi-cubic clusters. The appearance of boson peak, i. e., hump of C(T)/T3, verifies the existence of disordered phonon transports. Besides, the temperature dependence of \k{appa} can be described by classic Debye-Callaway model. Notably, above 350 K, the \k{appa} values of Re6Se8Te7 and Re6Te15 are remarkably close to the upper limit derived from glassy-like diffusion model. This finding sets the superatomic compounds as a promising family for searching ultralow-\k{appa} and energy management materials.

llm.relevance_to_user: 与增材制造力学性能研究方向完全无关，涉及超原子晶体的热导率

summary_zh.motivation: 探索超原子晶体的本征超低热导率
summary_zh.method: 生长高质量Re6Se8Te7和Re6Te15单晶并测量热导率
summary_zh.result: 室温热导率分别为0.32和0.53 W m-1 K-1，属于无机块体晶体中最低
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验测量和Debye-Callaway模型拟合验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the intrinsic ultralow thermal conductivity in superatomic bulk crystals.
summary_en.method: High-quality single crystals of Re6Se8Te7 and Re6Te15 were grown and their thermal conductivity was measured.
summary_en.result: Room-temperature thermal conductivities are 0.32 and 0.53 W m-1 K-1, among the lowest in all-inorganic bulk crystals.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements and Debye-Callaway model fitting.
